newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Johnson Electric says margins to improve.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Electric says margins to improve.

text.p: Johnson Electric said on Monday it expects operating margins to improve in fiscal 1996/97 due to lower prices of raw materials and a weaker yen.

"The lower prices of copper, steel and other materials as well as the weak yen have provided the company with a more favourable environment in which to operate in," chairman and chief executive Patrick Wang Shui-chung said in a statement.
"With improved operating margins, we remain optimistic about a good recovery in our earnings growth for the year 1996/97."
Johnson, a manufacturer of micro-motors, would benefit from a weaker yen because it gets much of its components from Japan.
Wang said the group's cost reduction and management initiatives have started to have a favourable impact on margins and earnings growth in the first half period.

With strong operating cash flow and reduced capital spending, the group's cash reserves increased to HK$1.98 billion in the first half on this year from HK$1.17 billion during the same period of fiscal 1995/96, the statement said.
But Wang said he expected slower sales growth in the second half, largely owing to lower output during the fourth quarter, which coincides with the Chinese New Year holiday period.
